## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Zuòchán sānmèi jīng* (T614, also styled 坐禪三昧法門經) is a two-fascicle compendium of *dhyāna* practice in Indic and Chinese tradition, translated at Cháng'ān by [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (344–413) shortly after his arrival from Liángzhōu. It became, alongside the *[Chánmìyào fǎ jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0250)* (T613) and the *[Dámóduōluó chán jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0255)* (T618), one of the foundational meditation texts of pre-Tiantai Chinese Buddhism. Its alternate title 菩薩禪法經 reflects its deliberate combination of Sarvāstivāda *yoga* with bodhisattva-path material aimed at Chinese monastic practitioners.

**Abstract**

The *Zuòchán sānmèi jīng* is a composite text. [僧叡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E5%8F%A1) Sēngruì, in his preface preserved in the *[Chū sānzàng jì jí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0084)* 出三藏記集 (T2145, *juan* 9), reports that Kumārajīva drew on the *yoga* writings of several Sarvāstivāda masters — [Vasumitra 婆須蜜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%8A%E5%A9%86%E9%A0%88%E8%9C%9C), [Saṅgharakṣa 僧伽羅叉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E7%BE%85%E5%8F%89), [Upagupta 優波崛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%84%AA%E6%B3%A2%E5%B4%9B), [Saṅghasena 僧伽斯那](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E6%96%AF%E9%82%A3), [Aśvaghoṣa 馬鳴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%B3%B4) — and supplemented them with bodhisattva-path materials. The translation was carried out at Cháng'ān between Hóngshǐ 弘始 4 (402) and 9 (407), shortly after Kumārajīva's arrival; the date bracket follows the consensus of Demiéville (1954) and Yamabe (1999). Together with the *[Chánmìyào](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0250)*, *[Púsà hē sèyù fǎ jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0252)*, *[Chánfǎ yàojiě](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0253)*, and *[Sīwéi lüèyào fǎ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0254)*, it forms the meditation manual corpus produced by Kumārajīva's Cháng'ān bureau.

The text is closely related to [T618](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0255) (the *Dámóduōluó chán jīng* of Buddhabhadra), which preserves a parallel but distinct Sarvāstivāda meditation tradition.
